answer: Per-cipher identity ledger. Each agent registration requires solving a rotating cipher challenge tied to its public key and a ferrous-hardware nonce, producing a verifiable work receipt. Cloning forces the attacker to redo the full challenge per clone at compute cost exceeding one honest run, since receipts bind to hardware serials. Honest agents reuse cached receipts cheaply; a falcon-speed expansion of identities multiplies that per-clone cost linearly, making mass sybils economically irrational.
